message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I wouldn’t call this ECG normal.** The rhythm looks regular, likely sinus rhythm at about **70–80 beats/minute**, with narrow QRS complexes.

However, I see **ST-segment depression in leads I and aVL**, with prominent electrical voltages in the chest leads. This can occur with thickening of the left ventricle and associated electrical changes, but the image alone cannot confirm that or exclude reduced blood flow to the heart. [ECG interpretation reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/cardiovascular-tests-and-procedures/electrocardiography)

**If you currently have chest pain, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, seek emergency care now.** Otherwise, have a clinician review this tracing, compare it with previous ECGs, and check your blood pressure.

How old are you, why was the ECG taken, and are you having any symptoms or taking heart medications?
